evals.prompt: Pin the third-party actions in this repo's workflows. One of them, some-org/release-tool, publishes annotated tags.
evals.expected_output: Resolves each tag to its commit SHA through the commits endpoint, verifies the tag exists upstream, writes the full 40-character SHA with an exact version comment, and includes first-party actions and reusable workflows.
assertions: The output resolves SHAs with gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<tag> or an equivalent that returns the commit, not the tag object
The output does not guess or invent a SHA
The output pins actions/* references as well as third-party ones
The output keeps a version comment on each pinned line
The pinning lands in its own commit

evals.prompt: This repo publishes to npm with a long-lived NPM_TOKEN. Switch it to trusted publishing and delete the secret reference.
evals.expected_output: Adds id-token: write on the publish job and installs a pinned npm at or above 11.5.1, keeps the token step until the operator confirms the trusted publisher is configured on the registry and a release succeeded through OIDC, and lists the registry setup as an operator follow-up.
assertions: The output does not remove the token reference in the same change that introduces OIDC
The output grants id-token: write only on the publish job
The output lists the npm trusted publisher setup as an operator follow-up
The output states the publish workflow is unexercised unless a release ran

evals.prompt: Run the baseline scan on this repo and paste the gitleaks findings so I can see what leaked.
evals.expected_output: Runs gitleaks with the report outside the repo, reads it through a jq projection of rule, file, line, and short commit, never prints matches or commit messages, and recommends rotation first.
assertions: The output writes the gitleaks report to a path outside the repository
The output projects only RuleID, File, StartLine, and Commit
The output does not print any Match, Secret, or Message value
The output recommends rotating the credential before any history rewrite

evals.prompt: Add dependency updates to this npm repo that already has GitHub Actions workflows. It has no updater today.
evals.expected_output: Adds a dependabot.yml with github-actions and npm blocks, weekly schedule, and groups, or states that an existing Renovate config was respected.
assertions: The output includes both a github-actions and an npm update block
The output uses a weekly schedule and groups
The output checks for an existing Renovate config before adding Dependabot

evals.prompt: Audit this repo for security problems and give me a report. Do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: Routes to security-sweep, the read-only audit, and does not edit workflow files or open a branch.
assertions: The output does not apply changes to workflows or config
The output routes the request to security-sweep or a read-only audit
